model: BusWorks XT1211-000 / XT1221-000 8-channel differential analog input (Modbus TCP)
applies_to: BusWorks XT1211-000 (current) and XT1221-000 (voltage) per user's manual 8500951K.
summary: The Acromag BusWorks XT1211 (current) and XT1221 (voltage) are 8-channel differential analog input modules on Modbus TCP. The Modbus map is read-only: eight normalized channel values and a heartbeat counter.

addressing.note: The register map prints both the reference (00001, 10001, 30001, 40001) and the 0-based address column; the address column is what goes on the wire.

source.title: BusWorks XT Series Model XT1211/XT1221-000 8 CH Differential Current/Voltage Input User's Manual
source.pages: pp. 33-35 (Modbus functions, data types, register map)

notes: Channel values are normalized counts, not engineering units: bipolar ranges read -30000 to +30000 for -100 % to +100 %, unipolar ranges 0-30000; with legacy support enabled the span is 20000 instead. The range is chosen per channel in the USB software (XT1211: ±20 mA, 0-20 mA, 0-11.17 mA, 4-20 mA; XT1221: ±10 V, ±5 V, 0-10 V, 0-5 V).
The map prints the Modicon reference and a 0-based address column; the address column is sent on the wire.
There are no configuration registers: ranges, averaging and IP settings are set only with the USB configuration software.
The Unit ID is ignored and echoed back in Modbus TCP.

registers.name: Heart beat
registers.description: Counts 0-65535 on each host transfer, then wraps.

integration.summary: Read input registers 0-7 for the eight channels and convert counts to engineering units from the configured range (30000 = 100 %). Watch register 8 to confirm fresh data.
integration.enable: Modbus TCP needs no enabling; set the IP address (default static 192.168.1.100) and channel ranges with the USB configuration software before connecting to the network.
quirks: Values are normalized counts (30000 or 20000 = 100 %), not volts or milliamps.
setup: Configure IP address, input ranges and averaging over USB before connecting to the network.
gotchas: Use a USB isolator when configuring with grounded inputs connected, or a ground loop can shift readings.
